problem_disposition.summary: CI needs to catch dead external links in this repo's Markdown docs before readers do, since a receipts-first repo that links to rotted evidence undermines its own premise. The reflex was to write a small custom checker script; deja-vu ran its own hunt on that reflex first.

candidate_comparisons.summary: async link checker, purpose-built for exactly this problem; official lychee-action wraps it for CI. Apache-2.0. Won on every declared dimension: CI-fit, activity, license, and built-in retry/rate-limit handling.

candidate_comparisons.summary: Active, ISC-licensed, CI-usable healthy runner-up, but Markdown-only (this repo's link surface isn't) and single-maintainer.
2,074★ but excluded by a dormancy criterion (no push since 2024-01) that was pre-registered before the sweep, not applied after seeing the star count.

Commodity plumbing (CI link-checking) fails the competency test and carries zero innovation-token justification — the hard parts (retries, rate limits, false-positive management) are exactly what a naive custom script would rediscover the hard way.

uncertainty.residual: none — quick-tier sweep found a clear category leader on every declared dimension; no evidence gap was carried forward

reversibility: high — dropping lychee is deleting one CI step, no data migration or API surface elsewhere depends on it

route_components.output_boundary: .github/workflows/ci.yml link-check job: pass/fail on every Markdown file's external links, using lycheeverse/lychee-action unmodified plus a .lycheeignore for known rate-limited hosts
policy_clauses: Apache-2.0 permits use via the published GitHub Action without redistributing/modifying lychee's source
accepted_obligations: maintain .lycheeignore for hosts that are known-rate-limited rather than actually dead
